assessments.reasoning: The trigger branch gives immediate dispatch and caller access to the returned value. The post branch queues the call on the object and makes the callee result inaccessible to the caller.

challenge.method: Compare the timing branches and stated restrictions on using a posted result as an expression or an argument. Challenge unconditional queue ordering with the nearby system-event caveat and compare older TriggerEvent and PostEvent APIs.
challenge.results: The result-access distinction survives the restrictions and timing caveat. Queue position can be affected by other work. Backward-compatible scheduling functions have their own argument rules, and their scheduling return conventions do not establish access to a posted callee result.

limitations: No promise about the next operation, the OS queue, reentrancy, or the return value from a scheduling helper is part of the finding.
